name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Ezell running with large fundraising edge
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Ezell's incumbency, and his roughly 34-to-1 fundraising advantage over Hulum leave the Democrat with no evident path; prediction markets price a Republican win at 96%. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending for Hulum or an unexpected Ezell scandal could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win would still require a major shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Mike Ezell seeks another term in this Gulf Coast district, which leans heavily Republican with a 21-point Republican advantage in recent partisan performance. Ezell was renominated without difficulty and has raised nearly a million dollars, leaving him with a large cash advantage. Democrat Jeffrey Hulum has raised under thirty thousand dollars, and an independent is also on the ballot.

No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, money, and markets, all of which point the same way. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 96 percent chance of holding the seat. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated even though a Democratic win would require an unusual late shift.
